newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Fuel shortages endanger Romania farming.
newsitem.headline: Fuel shortages endanger Romania farming.

text.p: Fuel shortages in Romania's farming sector over the past months could affect ploughing and harvesting, the agriculture minister said on Thursday.
Alexandru Lapusan told a news conference private and state-run farming enterprises had received 9,305 tonnes of diesel oil since October 1, "much lower than planned."
"We need 74,000 tonnes of diesel oil this month. Fuel supplies are already running behind schedule," Lapusan said.
Agricultural work has already been affected, especially ploughing and harvesting of sunflower, maize and sugarbeet, ministry sources said.
Delays in carrying out seasonal farm work might generate crop losses or endanger next year's crops, particularly in view of forecasts for an early winter, the sources said.
Romania has so far harvested 33 percent of its maize crop and 75 percent of sunflower.
Lapusan said fuel stocks in 19 counties had dwindled to zero, despite repeated promises by the National Oil Company (CRP) to supply enough fuel to the farm sector.
CRP officials were not available for comment.
Lapusan declined to comment on possible crop losses or delays caused by fuel shortages.
"It is hard to say how many days we've lost with harvesting or other work. All I can say is that the shortages are very disturbing," he said.
Last month, Romania had to dig into strategic fuel reserves to help the farming sector. Some 19,420 tonnes of diesel oil were taken from the National Material Reserves.
An acute hard currency shortage has forced Romania to cut crude oil imports over the summer months and distribution of fuel supplies has been disrupted across the country.
The government last month said it had guaranteed a $200 million loan for crude imports by the CRP over the coming months --Adrian Dascalu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
